## Highlights

- On **Auto**, a chat reply no longer ends when the provider of the chosen model refuses the message for the account: its credit is spent, it is limiting requests, it refuses the API key, or the plan does not include the model. Tale then picks a model from another provider, under the same governance and model access, and tries up to three models in all; the reply's details name the model that answered. A refusal of the message's content, which now includes a guardrail block or a flagged input, a refusal of its shape, a failure once the provider has accepted the message, and a model you chose yourself still end the reply. When every model refuses, the error names the provider that refused last and how many models were tried, and the hint for spent credit now suggests a model from another provider as well as more credits. Auto keeps nothing between messages: the next one may pick the refusing provider first again ([#5339](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5339)). See [Choose automatic or explicit selection](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/models#choose-automatic-or-explicit-selection).
- An AI gateway's image models can be selected for image generation. A model that a gateway such as Bifrost lists without saying what it does, by its id, context window and price alone, that Tale's catalogs don't know, and whose name says it creates images, such as `gemini-3.1-flash-image`, is now offered for image generation under **Settings › Governance › Models**, and no longer in the chat's model picker. An image model that Tale's own catalogs know, such as `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, which such a listing left out of both pickers, is offered there too. When the gateway refuses to create the image through its images API, as Bifrost does for the image models it routes to OpenRouter ("image_generation is not supported by openrouter provider"), Tale asks the same model for the image through Chat Completions, and asks there first for up to a day. A model Tale's catalogs don't know draws from the prompt alone: Tale gives it no picture to start from. **Automatic** never picks a gateway's image model: select one to use it. See [Define a custom provider](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/providers#define-a-custom-provider) and [Allow image generation](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/governance/content-models#let-agents-generate-images).
- Replacing an API key made for a team or for the organization no longer strands the conversations it [mirrors](https://docs.tale.dev/develop/api-reference#mirror-conversations-and-deliver-replies). A mirror now belongs to the integration that created it, which is whom the key belongs to: the new key continues the existing mirrors, lists them and claims the replies queued for them before the swap, where it was refused with `INTEGRATION_NOT_OWNED`. A personal key and a key made for a member act as that person, and a key that belongs to someone else is still refused. Two keys made for the same team or organization now share their mirrors and the replies queued for them; to keep two integrations apart, give each its own team or member. An upload stays with the key that staged it ([#5007](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5007)).
- **Test connection** for an organization's knowledge database under **Settings › Data residency** now judges TLS as the saved connection does. With **SSL mode** `prefer`, a database that serves no TLS passed the test and was then never reached, so a later save of another embedding model was refused; it now fails the test. With `verify-ca` or `verify-full`, a server whose certificate a CA in `POSTGRES_CA_FILE` signed, such as Amazon RDS's, failed the test although the connection worked; it now passes ([#5330](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/5330)).
- Uploads no longer slow down in an organization whose file storage refuses to delete files: the cleanup each upload runs now checks at most 25 expired upload records at a time, oldest first, where it checked all of them. Two Inbox replies, API conversation snapshots or task saves sent at the same moment that attach the same uploaded files in a different order no longer deadlock, which failed one of them.
- **Session Manager** is released for the first time, as the image `ghcr.io/tale-project/tale/tale-session-manager`. It runs isolated browser sessions on your own computer, each a Camoufox browser with its own profile, fingerprint and proxy, which you use in a web page and AI assistants use through MCP. It runs on its own, from `compose.session-manager.yml`, which publishes it on the loopback address only. It has no login, so keep it there, or put a reverse proxy that authenticates in front of it. Data of the earlier Python app is not migrated ([#5332](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5332)). Its [README](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/tree/main/services/session-manager#run-it-in-docker) says how to run the released image.

## Upgrade notes

- At start, the backend applies `0235_conversation_api_source_owners.sql`. It adds the owning integration to each API-mirrored conversation's binding and fills it, within the binding's organization, for the bindings that keys made for a team or the organization created; every other binding belongs to its person, as before. A trigger fills it for the bindings the previous image creates during a rolling deploy. The API contract stays at `3.52.0`.
- Replace a team's or the organization's API key only once every backend runs this release: until then, the previous image still refuses the new key on the mirrors the old one created.
- If **Test connection** now fails for an organization's knowledge database with **SSL mode** `prefer`, either the database serves no TLS or `POSTGRES_CA_FILE` names a file the backend cannot read, and Tale could not reach the database in that mode before this release either: turn on TLS for the database or fix the file, or choose `disable` where the network to the database is trusted.
- A gateway's image model is no longer a chat model, and a request that names one as its chat model is refused: choose a chat model for a chat, an agent or a default-model rule set to one. For the image models a Bifrost gateway routes to OpenRouter, the gateway needs Bifrost 2.4.0 or later: an older Bifrost drops the image, and the request fails saying the model answered without one. An image from a gateway model whose listing gives no price, and whose reply reports none, is booked at no cost, since Tale guesses no price.
- `tale deploy` neither pulls nor starts the Session Manager, so an existing deployment needs no change for it.
- No configuration, limit, credential or sign-in setting needs to change beyond these: the other fixes take effect with the new images.
